_comment: Optional: holidays Celebrated in individual provinces rather than across
Tamriel as a whole. High Rock, Hammerfell, Morrowind, Elsweyr and
Summerset, drawn from Arena and Daggerfall era lore.
Install this alongside 10_Vanilla.json for a full calendar, or leave
it out to see only the holidays Skyrim itself would keep.
No date here collides with one in 10_Vanilla.json, so the two can be
used together with one holiday per day.
DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE to add your own events -- add your own instead.

events.name: Scour Day
events.description: Most High Rock villages clean up after New Life. What began as tidying has long since become a party of its own. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Ovank'a
events.description: The people of the Alik'r Desert offer prayers to Stendarr for a mild and merciful year. It is considered very holy. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: The Day of Lights
events.description: The villages of the Iliac Bay pray for a good farming and fishing year. It is taken very seriously. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: Waking Day
events.description: Invented in Yeorth Burrowland to wake the spirits of nature after a long winter, and grown into a riotous celebration of its end. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Mad Pelagius
events.description: A mock memorial in High Rock to Pelagius Septim III, one of the maddest emperors in history. The Septims since have taken it in good humour. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Othroktide
events.description: Dwynnen celebrates the day Baron Othrok took the land back from the undead forces at the Battle of Wightmoor. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Day of Release
events.description: The people of Glenumbra Moors may be the only ones who still mark the battle between Aiden Direnni and the Alessian Army. They do so vigorously. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Perseverance Day
events.description: Once a solemn memorial in Ykalon to those killed resisting the Camoran Usurper, now a boisterous festival. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Aduros Nau
events.description: The villages of the Bantha mark the baser urges of springtide. The traditions vary, and none of them are for the overly virtuous. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: The Day of Waiting
events.description: An old holy day in the Dragontail Mountains. A dragon is said to come from the desert to devour the wicked, so everyone locks themselves inside. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: Hogithum
events.description: The day the Dunmer priesthoods formally summon Azura for her guidance and support. Celebrated in Morrowind.

events.name: Flower Day
events.description: Children pick the first flowers of spring while older Bretons, cooped up all winter, come out to dance and sing. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Festival of Blades
events.description: The Alik'r celebrates the first Redguard's victory over a race of giant goblins. Scholars call it myth; the desert celebrates anyway. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: Gardtide
events.description: Tamarilyn Point honours Druagaa, the old goddess of flowers. Her worship is all but dead, but the festival is always a success. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: The Day of the Dead
events.description: One of Daggerfall's stranger holidays. The superstitious say the dead rise to take vengeance on the living, and it was on this day that King Lysandus's spectre began its haunting. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: The Day of Shame
events.description: No one on the Hammerfell coast leaves their house. The Crimson Ship, filled with plague victims refused refuge centuries ago, is said to return. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: Rite of Vigyld
events.description: A rite of the Psijic Order, meant to empower salutary spirits and debilitate unclean ones. Celebrated in Summerset.

events.name: Marukh's Day
events.description: Observed in Skeffington Wood alone. By measuring themselves against the prophet Marukh, its people pray for the strength to resist temptation. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: The Fire Festival
events.description: One of the best attended celebrations in High Rock. Northmoor's ancient display of magic and military strength has become a festival. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Fishing Day
events.description: The Bretons of the Iliac Bay are not usually a flamboyant people, but on Fishing Day they make enough noise to scare the fish away for weeks. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Drigh R'Zimb
events.description: Held in Abibon-Gora at the hottest time of year, a jubilation for the sun itself. The Redguards may have brought it with them in the first era. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: Dancing Day
events.description: A time-honoured holiday in Daggerfall, popularised by the Red Prince Atryck. An occasion of great pomp from the nobles down. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Tibedetha
events.description: 'Tiber's Day'. Alcaire celebrates its most famous native, though Tiber Septim never once returned to his birthplace. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Divad Etep't
events.description: Antiphyllos mourns Divad, son of Frandar, one of the greatest early Redguard heroes. Historians question his deeds; his tomb is almost certainly genuine. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: Fiery Night
events.description: Few but the natives of the Alik'r would venture out on the hottest day of the year. Its meaning is lost to antiquity; the celebration is not. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: The Day of Maiden Katrica
events.description: Ayasofya throws its biggest party of the year for the warrior who saved the county. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: Koomu Alezer'i
events.description: 'We Acknowledge' in old Redguard. Whatever the harvest, Sentinel thanks the gods for their bounty and prays to be worthy of it. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: The Feast of the Tiger
events.description: A harvest holiday in the Bantha rainforest, kept not with solemn thanksgiving but with celebration from village to village. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: Appreciation Day
events.description: An ancient thanksgiving in Anticlere for a bountiful harvest. A holy and contemplative day, devoted to Mara. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: The Rites of Moawita
events.description: A Psijic Order rite for empowering salutary spirits and debilitating unclean ones. Celebrated in Summerset.

events.name: Khurat
events.description: The Wrothgarian Mountains mark the day their finest young scholars enter the priesthoods. Even those without children of age pray for the wisdom of the clergy. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Riglametha
events.description: Lainlyn celebrates its many blessings with pageants, among them the Ghraewaj, when the city's daedra worshippers were turned to harpies for their blasphemy. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: Children's Day
events.description: A festive day in Betony with a grim root: it began as a memorial to the children taken from their homes by vampires a century ago. It is now a celebration of youth. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Dirij Tereur
events.description: The Alik'r honours Frandar Hunding, who led the Redguards to Hammerfell in the first era. Stories are read from his Book of Circles and the temples fill to capacity. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: Day of the Pariah
events.description: The day the Orcs of Wrothgar and strongholds across Tamriel formally seek the guidance and favor of Malacath, the Daedric Prince of the Outcasts. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Broken Diamonds
events.description: Glenpoint remembers the empress Kintyra Septim II, who died in its dungeons on the order of a usurper. A day of silent prayer for the wisdom of the imperial family. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: The Serpent's Dance
events.description: Satakalaam's great street festival. Whether it began as a holy day to a snake god is no longer clear, and no longer matters. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: Moon Festival
events.description: Glenumbra Moors honours Secunda, goddess of the moon. She has no active worshippers, but the feasting has continued through the ages. Celebrated in High Rock.

events.name: Hel Anseilak
events.description: 'Communion with the Saints of the Sword'. The most serious of holy days in Pothago. The way of Hel Ansei is no longer practised, but its heritage is honoured. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: Baranth Do
events.description: 'Goodbye to the Beast of Last Year'. The Alik'r parades demonic representations of the old year, and revels to honour the new. Celebrated in Hammerfell.

events.name: Chil'a
events.description: The blessing of the new year in the barony of Kairou, at once sacred and festive. The archpriest and baroness consecrate the ashes of the old year, then the parades and tournaments begin. Celebrated in Hammerfell.
